interpretation: Projected attack paths: not confirmed attacks, and not a likelihood assessment. An LLM placed techniques that MITRE ATT&CK documents this actor using onto the organization's own flow map, reasoning the way an adversary would. Technique ids, technique names and controls are sourced; the route, the step rationales and the access states are the model's projection. Each step's access is checked only for continuity — that an earlier step produced what the step needs — never for truth. A step that states no access falls back to a typical value for its tactic.

scenarios.name: Volt Typhoon (G1017) vs Claims Portal: portal-api-docstore
scenarios.description: Volt Typhoon exploits the internet-facing portal, steals API credentials, establishes a proxy, and accesses the unauthenticated document store.
scenarios.attack_objective: Exfiltrate PII from the unauthenticated S3 document store.

attack_sequence.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: The Claims portal is exposed to the internet and runs Django, making it vulnerable to web application exploits that target business logic or framework flaws.
success_indicators: The attacker achieves arbitrary code execution on the portal server.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker can route malicious HTTP requests to the public portal.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The portal runs complex application code with a public interface that accepts untrusted input.
assumptions: The application contains an exploitable RCE vulnerability.
attack_sequence.control_note: The implemented WAF only provides partial protection with a low bypass difficulty, easily circumvented using payload obfuscation.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has gained initial access through exploitation of multiple vulnerabilities in internet-facing software and appliances such as Fortinet, Ivanti (formerly Pulse Secure), NETGEAR, Citrix,…

attack_sequence.name: Unix Shell on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: Volt Typhoon heavily utilizes built-in command interpreters; a Unix shell allows them to interact natively with the portal's underlying Linux OS.
success_indicators: The attacker gains interactive command execution capabilities on the host.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has successfully executed an initial exploit payload.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The web application runs in an environment with standard Unix utilities and shell binaries available.
assumptions: The web service account has sufficient OS permissions to spawn a shell.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has used Brightmetricagent.exe which contains a command- line interface (CLI) library that can leverage command shells including Z Shell (zsh).

attack_sequence.name: Unsecured Credentials on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: To move laterally to the internal API, the attacker searches the Django configuration files and environment variables for plaintext API tokens.
success_indicators: The attacker possesses valid OAuth2 credentials for the backend API.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker can read configuration files on the portal's filesystem.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The portal stores OAuth2 credentials required for authenticating to the Claims API in a recoverable format.
assumptions: OAuth2 tokens or client secrets are stored unencrypted on disk or in the environment.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has obtained credentials insecurely stored on targeted network appliances.

attack_sequence.name: Internal Proxy on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: By setting up an internal proxy, Volt Typhoon creates a reliable C2 tunnel to route traffic securely into the restricted internal network.
success_indicators: The attacker has an active network tunnel into the internal app zone.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has OS access and needs to direct traffic to internal components.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The portal is explicitly permitted to route HTTPS traffic to the internal claims_api.
assumptions: Egress and ingress filtering on the edge zone permits the proxy connection to persist.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has used the built-in netsh `port proxy` command to create proxies on compromised systems to facilitate access.

attack_sequence.name: Valid Accounts on Claims API
attack_sequence.description: Routing traffic through the portal proxy, the attacker presents the stolen OAuth2 tokens to authenticate to the Claims API.
success_indicators: The attacker gains authenticated application-level access to the internal API.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker holds the valid OAuth2 token and can route to the API via the proxy.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The API relies entirely on the OAuth2 token for trust and does not restrict requests to specific trusted IP origins.
assumptions: The OAuth2 token is valid and lacks sender-constrained binding.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon relies primarily on valid credentials for persistence.

attack_sequence.name: File and Directory Discovery on Document store
attack_sequence.description: Using the authenticated API session, the attacker queries API endpoints that interact with the unauthenticated S3 document store to map out available files.
success_indicators: The attacker successfully discovers the directory structure and locations of PII files.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker is authenticated to the API which has direct unauthenticated access to the document store.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The internal network allows the API to read from the document store without requiring individual user authentication.
assumptions: The API exposes functionality that can be manipulated to list backend file directories.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has enumerated directories containing vulnerability testing and cyber related content and facilities data such as construction drawings.
attack_sequence.state_check: gap — needs network_reach on doc_store; no earlier step reaches it. Path holds service_credential

attack_sequence.name: Local Data Staging on Document store
attack_sequence.description: Volt Typhoon initiates reads of the targeted PII documents from the S3 bucket, staging them temporarily for exfiltration.
success_indicators: The attacker successfully accesses and collects the PII data.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker knows the specific file paths of the sensitive PII documents.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The document store lacks data-level access controls for the unauthenticated requests coming from the API.
assumptions: The API can be coerced into returning the raw contents of the documents to the portal.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has saved stolen files including the `ntds.dit` database and the `SYSTEM` and `SECURITY` Registry hives locally to the `C:\Windows\Temp\` directory.

scenarios.name: Volt Typhoon (G1017) vs Claims Portal: portal-api-claimsdb
scenarios.description: Volt Typhoon drops a web shell on the portal, initiates protocol tunneling, and leverages the API to discover the regulated claims database.
scenarios.attack_objective: Map out and access the restricted claims database by pivoting through the application tier.

attack_sequence.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: Exploiting the public-facing Django portal provides the initial foothold required to bypass perimeter security.
success_indicators: The attacker achieves initial code execution on the web server.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker can send crafted HTTP payloads to the public portal.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The portal has an internet-exposed web application vulnerable to exploitation.
assumptions: An exploitable vulnerability exists in the Django application or its dependencies.
attack_sequence.control_note: The low bypass WAF fails to identify and block the initial exploitation vector.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has gained initial access through exploitation of multiple vulnerabilities in internet-facing software and appliances such as Fortinet, Ivanti (formerly Pulse Secure), NETGEAR, Citrix,…

attack_sequence.name: Web Shell on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: Volt Typhoon frequently relies on web shells for persistence; installing one ensures reliable re-entry to the compromised portal.
success_indicators: The attacker secures long-term persistent access to the portal.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has code execution and can write files to the web directory.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The Django web server processes executable files or templates dropped into web-accessible directories.
assumptions: The web server configuration allows the execution of dropped shell scripts.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has used webshells, including ones named AuditReport.jspx and iisstart.aspx, in compromised environments.

attack_sequence.name: Unsecured Credentials on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: Extracting the configured API OAuth2 tokens from the portal's configuration is necessary to traverse the semi-trusted zone boundary.
success_indicators: The attacker extracts the OAuth2 token required for the Claims API.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has persistent shell access to the portal.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The application relies on static or long-lived tokens stored locally to talk to the API.
assumptions: The credentials are left in plain text within reachable configuration files.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has obtained credentials insecurely stored on targeted network appliances.

attack_sequence.name: Protocol Tunneling on Claims portal
attack_sequence.description: Using tools like FRP, the attacker tunnels custom protocols over the HTTP C2 channel to orchestrate the internal network pivot.
success_indicators: The attacker establishes a protocol tunnel to proxy tools deep into the architecture.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has deployed a persistence mechanism and has execution rights.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The portal supports outgoing network connections and complex data payloads over standard web ports.
assumptions: Firewalls do not deeply inspect or block non-standard traffic tunneled via HTTP.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: FRP can tunnel SSH and Unix Domain Socket communications over TCP between external nodes and exposed resources behind firewalls or NAT.

attack_sequence.name: Valid Accounts on Claims API
attack_sequence.description: Passing the stolen API tokens through the established protocol tunnel grants authenticated access to the internal Claims API.
success_indicators: The attacker successfully authenticates to the Claims API.
attack_sequence.precondition: The protocol tunnel is active and the attacker has the OAuth2 credentials.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The Claims API exposes sensitive internal functions via HTTPS and trusts valid OAuth2 tokens.
assumptions: API token validation does not require multi-factor authentication or source IP verification.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon relies primarily on valid credentials for persistence.

attack_sequence.name: Network Service Discovery on Claims database
attack_sequence.description: Operating through the API, the attacker enumerates the restricted database schemas and connectivity to locate the regulated data.
success_indicators: The attacker maps the claims database structure and confirms access to regulated data tables.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker is fully authenticated to the API which has Postgres access to the claims database.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The database uses mTLS with the API, allowing any API-driven logic flaw to interact directly with the database.
assumptions: The API allows arbitrary SQL injection or expansive data querying.
attack_sequence.control_note: The database firewall has a medium bypass rating, which the attacker circumvents by hiding within the legitimate mTLS tunnel from the API.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Volt Typhoon has used commercial tools, LOTL utilities, and appliances already present on the system for network service discovery.
